title: Wet Sand Letters
lesson: Letter shapes and letter sounds, finger control
scene: Top-down view of a giant capital letter pressed as a wide groove into wet river sand. A glowing pebble marks the start, and a sparkling yellow trail follows the child's finger while the Orbi hums the letter's sound.

views.world: A wide river beach of smooth round pebbles and dark wet sand in soft morning light. Clear shallow water ripples over stones. Blue-green trees lean over the bank, holding small white lattice nests in their crowns. Far away a slim white Chord tower rises, twisted like a plant stem, its rings catching the sun. Calm, cool and quiet.
views.details: Linky, a round chibi friend with a coral-red left eye and a sky-blue right eye, sits in the sand with his red and blue hands ready. A white Orbi sphere floats above with a soft glowing equator. The letter grooves are damp and shiny brown, the trail glows sunshine yellow, and soft gray outlines keep every shape big and clear.
views.discovery: Each finished letter turns into a little picture made of sand and pebbles: a curling S becomes a stream, an O becomes a pond with a fish. Later the river gently smooths the sand so new letters can appear, then lowercase partners, and finally the first letter of the child's own name, framed by pebbles.

story: Linky wanted to make a letter in the sand. He pressed too fast, and the line went wobbly. The river came up softly and smoothed the sand flat again. "Try again, slowly," hummed his Orbi. Linky started at the glowing pebble. He went down, around, and down again. The line was slow and round and good. The letter shone, and the Orbi sang its sound. This time the river did not wash it away. It waited beside the letter, as if it wanted to listen too.
wisdom: Slow lines make strong letters.

title: Footprint Numbers
genre: Number tracing and counting to ten
lesson: Numerals 1 to 10, one-to-one counting
scene: A huge numeral three lies as a wide path of soft sand on the beach. The child traces it with one finger, then three fluffy river chicks waddle onto the path, and each one cheeps when tapped and counted.

views.world: The pebble beach at midday, warm and bright, with gentle river water sparkling at the edge. Reeds sway in small clumps, and sandpipers dash along the waterline. White lattice nests rest in leafy trees on the far bank. A thin white Chord tower stands beyond the trees under a pale blue sky with puffy clouds. Wide, low camera, cheerful mood.
views.details: Fluffy gray-and-cream river chicks with orange feet leave tiny footprints in the sand. The Beadles, little bead-chain creatures, stand beside the path, the Beadle of three with three shiny beads. A white Orbi floats near the numeral, its coral-red and sky-blue eyes blinking. Sand is warm beige, footprints darker, outlines soft gray.
views.discovery: Numbers grow from one to ten. After each trace, the right number of chicks, baby turtles or grazer fawns walks the path, and the child counts them by tapping each once. Later the Beadle of each number joins the line, and the finished numerals stay along the river as a long trail of footprints and friends.

story: Three river chicks wanted to walk to the water, but they kept getting lost in the sand. "I will draw you a path," said the Beadle of three. He drew a big curly three in the sand, slowly, from the top. One chick stepped on. Then two. Then three. "One, two, three!" the Beadle counted, and touched each fluffy head once, never twice. The chicks marched along the curly path and splashed into the shallows. Every one was counted, and no one was left behind.
wisdom: Count each friend once, and no one is missed.

title: First Sound Boats
lesson: Hearing the first sound of a word, early phonics
scene: Three broad leaf boats drift slowly in a calm river pool, each carrying a big picture: a ball, a fish and a moon. The Orbi says a sound, and the child taps the boat whose picture starts with it.

views.world: A quiet bend of the river where the water forms a round, calm pool between smooth boulders. Willows drip light green leaves onto the surface, and small white lattice nests peek from their branches. A white Chord tower stands far upstream, misty in soft afternoon light. Dragonflies hover, and the pool reflects a pale blue sky.
views.details: Leaf boats are broad green leaves with curled edges, each carrying one large, clear picture of a familiar thing. Letterlinks, little letter creatures holding hands, wave from a flat rock. A white Orbi hovers low over the water, its coral-red left eye and sky-blue right eye glowing as it speaks. Soft green, water blue and sunny yellow.
views.discovery: At first the boats carry very different sounds, like m, s and b. Later the sounds come closer, and four boats float at once. Each found boat sails to a little harbor of stones, where words that start alike wait together. Tapping the harbor plays them back, and the matching Letterlink rides on top.

story: The Orbi hummed a sound over the pool. "Mmm." Three leaf boats came drifting. One carried a fish, one a ball, and one a moon. Little Letterlink M listened to each one. "Fish. Fff. Not me." "Ball. Buh. Not me." "Moon. Mmm!" M hopped onto the moon boat and laughed. "I knew it was you. Your name starts like my sound." The boat sailed to the stone harbor, where all the M words were waiting, humming together like bees.
wisdom: Listen to the start, and words tell their names.

title: Rhyming Twins
lesson: Hearing rhymes, playing with sounds
scene: Soru holds a big picture of a cat. Three pictures float beside Tari: a hat, a cup and a tree. The child drags the hat to Tari, and the twins hold hands as a glowing arrow appears between them.

views.world: A sunny sandbar in the middle of the river, ringed by round pebbles and shallow, glittering water. Tall reeds and one blue-green tree with a white lattice nest give soft shade. On the far shore a white Chord tower rises beside a gentle hill. The light is warm and golden, and small fish flash in the shallows.
views.details: Soru is a coral-red round blob and Tari a sky-blue square blob, both chibi with big low eyes and soft gray outlines. A glowing red-to-blue arrow links their hands. The floating pictures sit on round pebble discs. A white Orbi rests in the sand like a quiet ball, eyes half open. Coral, sky blue, sand and soft green.
views.discovery: Rhyme families grow from pairs like cat and hat to chains like bee, tree and key. Later Soru says a word and the child chooses from four pictures. In a song mode the twins sing a short silly rhyme on the sandbar and pause, and the child taps the picture that finishes the line.

story: Soru held up a picture of a cat. "Cat!" she said. Tari looked at a cup, a tree and a hat. "Cup? No, that sounds different. Tree? No." Then Tari picked up the hat. "Cat, hat! Cat, hat!" The twins laughed and held hands, and an arrow glowed between them. "Our words sound like friends," said Soru. "They end the same way," said Tari, "just like our arrow." They hopped on the sandbar singing cat, hat, sat, until the little fish came up to listen.
wisdom: Words that end alike are friends.

title: Rela's Two Sides
lesson: Opposites: big and small, full and empty, up and down
scene: Rela, a round two-faced moon creature, floats over the beach showing a full basket of berries. Three big picture pebbles wait below: an empty basket, a tree and a fish. The child taps the empty basket, and Rela turns around to show it.

views.world: The pebble beach at dusk, when the sky turns peach and lilac. The two small moons, Pim and Pom, rise above the river. A white Chord tower glows softly at its crown, dimmed for the animals. Trees on the bank hold white lattice nests lit by tiny warm lights. The water is calm and mirror-smooth. Wide, quiet composition.
views.details: Rela is a friendly chibi moon with a pale cream front face and a soft blue back face, each with big gentle eyes. Picture pebbles are chunky, round and smooth, each showing one clear image. A white Orbi floats beside Rela, its coral-red and sky-blue eyes reflected in the water. Soft gray outlines; peach, lilac, cream and blue.
views.discovery: Pairs grow from big and small to in and out, wet and dry, fast and slow, near and far. Later the child acts out opposites by dragging: a frog jumps into the pond, then out again. A night round uses the moons Pim and Pom, one bright and one in shadow, to show light and dark.

story: Rela the moon has two faces. On one side she is bright and wide awake. On the other side she is dark and sleepy. A little crab asked, "Which one is the real you?" Rela smiled with both faces. "Both. I am full and I am empty. I am up and I am down. Every side needs its other side." The crab thought about it. "Then I am awake now, and sleepy later, and still me." "Yes," said Rela, and turned around to show him the stars.
wisdom: Every side has another side.

title: Stepping Stone Patterns
lesson: Repeating patterns, predicting what comes next
scene: Side view of round stepping stones crossing a shallow stream in a red, blue, red, blue pattern with one gap. The child drags the right colored stone into the gap, and Linky hops across with a happy boop.

views.world: A shallow, sparkling stream runs across the pebble beach to join the river. Green moss and tiny white flowers grow between the stones. Blue-green trees with white lattice nests frame the scene, and a white Chord tower rises in the soft distance. Morning light is clear and gentle, with dew on every leaf.
views.details: Stepping stones are round, smooth and big, colored coral red, sky blue and leaf green, with soft gray outlines and one gentle shadow. Linky waits on the near bank, his red and blue hands raised. A white Orbi hovers over the gap, lifting the chosen stone with a faint shimmer. The water is clear turquoise over pale pebbles.
views.discovery: Patterns grow from AB to ABB, AAB and ABC, first with colors, then with round and square shapes, then with sounds, where each stone plays a note. Later the child lays a whole pattern path, and Soru, Tari and Verbi hop across it in a line, humming the pattern out loud as they go.

story: Linky wanted to cross the stream. The stones went red, blue, red, blue, red, and then there was a gap. "Which one comes next?" asked the Orbi. Linky looked back along the path. "Red, blue, red, blue, red," he sang. "Blue!" The Orbi lifted a blue stone and set it gently in the gap. Linky hopped across. On the other side he turned and looked at the path. It was like a song he could see. "Patterns tell me what comes next," he said.
wisdom: Look back, and you will know what comes next.

title: Four Nest Sorting
lesson: Sorting by color and shape together, classification
scene: A tree holds four white lattice nests in a square: red round, red square, blue round and blue square. The child drags a small blue square cushion into the blue square nest, and it settles with a soft puff.

views.world: A big blue-green tree on the riverbank with wide, low branches. Four woven white nests sit in a neat square among the leaves, and sunlight filters through in warm spots. Below, round pebbles cover the beach and the river glints. A white Chord tower stands far off, its rings shining softly. Front view, calm and tidy.
views.details: The nests are woven from white lattice, two with coral-red rims and two with sky-blue rims, two round and two square. Items to sort are soft cushions, wooden blocks and toy balls in clear colors and shapes. Soru and Tari sit on a branch to cheer. A white Orbi floats by the trunk, lifting items with a shimmer.
views.discovery: First one rule at a time: color only, then shape only. Then both together in the four nests. Later size joins as a third idea with big and small items, and the child can invent a secret rule for the twins to guess. A tidy-up round brings every item back to its own place.

story: The wind tossed the nest cushions everywhere. Soru said, "Red ones go in red nests!" Tari said, "Square ones go in square nests!" They began to argue. Then Verbi jumped between them. "Look! This one is red and square. Where does it go?" The twins looked up at the tree. One nest was red and square. "There!" they said together. They sorted every cushion by color and by shape. When they finished, each nest was cozy, and the twins were laughing again.
wisdom: Two ideas together find the right place.

title: Little Paths Home
lesson: Planning a path, finger control, trying again
scene: High view of a wide sandy path winding between reeds and pebbles. The child slides one finger along it, guiding a fluffy river chick from the water's edge to its mother's nest in the grass.

views.world: A sunny stretch of riverbank where tall reeds and pebble mounds make gentle curving lanes. Butterflies drift across a bright sky. White lattice nests hang in the trees above, and a white Chord tower stands beyond them. The light is warm and wide, and the river shines softly at the bottom of the picture.
views.details: The path is wide pale sand with soft edges, three finger widths across. A gray-and-cream river chick with orange feet follows the finger, peeping. Reeds are green with brown tufts. A white Orbi hovers ahead as a guide, eyes glowing coral red and sky blue, and Itsy, the hugging loop friend, waits at the nest.
views.discovery: Mazes grow from one bend to two or three choices, then to little loops with stepping stones and log bridges. At a dead end the chick turns around with a giggle and a voiced hint, never a failure. Later the child can draw a new path for a friend and choose which baby animal goes home next.

story: A little river chick wandered off to see the water. When it turned around, it saw only reeds. "Peep?" it said. The Orbi floated down. "I know the way, but you can find it too. Follow the sand." The chick walked one way and met a rock. It walked another way and met the water. Then it found the soft sand path between the reeds and followed it, turn by turn, to its mother's nest. Itsy was waiting there with a hug. "You found your own way home," she said.
wisdom: A wrong turn helps you learn the road.

title: Big Piece Pictures
lesson: Part and whole, shapes and spatial thinking
scene: Six big puzzle pieces lie on a flat beach stone beside a faint outline of a grazer fawn. The child drags a piece near its place, it snaps in with a click, and the finished picture starts to move.

views.world: A flat white boulder on the pebble beach serves as a puzzle table. Behind it the river flows slowly, and grazers drink on the far shore. Trees hold white lattice nests, and a white Chord tower rises over the forest. Soft afternoon light, long gentle shadows, and a calm, focused mood. Slightly raised camera over the stone.
views.details: Pieces are thick and rounded with big tabs, like wooden toys, showing bright pictures of Raya's animals and places. A faint gray ghost outline shows where each piece belongs. Akoren, a tiny glowing acorn in warm orange and icy blue, watches from the stone. A white Orbi lifts pieces with a shimmer. Warm wood, sand and soft green.
views.discovery: Puzzles grow from 6 to 9 to 12 pieces, and the ghost outline fades as the child gets better. Each finished picture comes alive: a fawn drinks, a heron flies, a tower glows at night. Later finished puzzles hang in a gallery nest in the trees, and a silly mode swaps pieces between two pictures.

story: Akoren found pieces scattered on the big stone. A leg here, an ear there, a tail far away. "What a puzzle," he laughed slowly. He turned one piece, then another. A tail fit next to a back. An ear fit next to a head. Slowly, slowly, a little fawn appeared. When the last piece clicked in, the fawn blinked and stood up on wobbly legs. "Big things are made of small pieces," said Akoren. "And every small piece has its own place."
wisdom: Every small piece has its own place.

title: Peek Under Pebbles
lesson: Visual and sound memory, matching
scene: Eight big round pebbles lie scattered on the sand. The Orbi lifts one to reveal a tiny frog that croaks, then the child taps another pebble and finds the matching frog, and both hop happily.

views.world: A sunlit patch of beach where large smooth pebbles rest on soft sand near the river's edge. Small waves lap the shore. Blue-green trees with white lattice nests stand behind, and a white Chord tower rises far away. The sky is soft blue with a few fluffy clouds. Top-down camera, playful and calm.
views.details: Pebbles are big, round and gray-blue, with a soft shine. Under them hide chibi animal friends: frogs, crabs, snails and baby turtles, each with its own sound. A white Orbi hovers above, lifting pebbles with a gentle shimmer, coral-red and sky-blue eyes bright. Postie Index, the mail-carrier snail, watches from a flat stone.
views.discovery: Rounds grow from 6 to 8 to 12 pebbles. Found pairs stay out and play together at the water's edge. Later a listening round hides friends that are only heard, not seen. Every round ends with a tidy-up, where the Orbi puts each pebble back exactly where it lay, because the beach should stay as it was.

story: Under the pebbles, little friends were playing hide and seek. The Orbi lifted one pebble. A frog said, "Ribbit!" and ducked back down. The Orbi lifted another. A crab waved and hid again. "Where is the frog's twin?" asked Postie the snail. "The ribbit came from over here," said the Orbi, and lifted a pebble near the first. Two frogs hopped out and hugged. When all the friends were found, the Orbi set every pebble back just where it was, as if no one had played there at all.
wisdom: Leave the beach as you found it.

title: Twin Nests
lesson: Careful looking, same and different
scene: Two white lattice nests hang side by side on one branch. They look the same, but one holds a blue ball and the other an empty cushion. The child taps the empty cushion, and it sparkles.

views.world: A large blue-green tree leaning over the pebble beach, with two matching white lattice nests hanging from one branch like lanterns. The river glitters below, and a white Chord tower stands tall in the distance. Late morning light shines through the leaves in dappled spots. Birds sing, and the mood is cozy and curious.
views.details: The nests are round, woven from white lattice with green trims and round windows. Inside are cushions, toy blocks and a sleepy owl chick. Uni, a little sparkle with one big eye, peeks from a leaf. A white Orbi floats between the nests, glowing gently. Differences are big and clear: a missing toy, a color swap, a moved cushion.
views.discovery: First one big difference, then two, then three. If the child looks for a while, a voiced hint makes the right nest wiggle. Later the nests show seasons, with snow on one roof and blossoms on the other, and the child can make a change in one nest for a friend to find.

story: Two nests hung on the same branch. "They are twins," said the owl chick. Uni blinked her one big eye. "Almost twins. Look closely." The chick looked. Both nests had a white roof. Both had a round window. Both had a red cushion. But one nest had a little blue ball inside, and the other did not. "There!" said the chick. Uni sparkled. "Things can look the same, but each one is its own." The chick rolled the blue ball across, so both nests could play.
wisdom: Look slowly, and small things become big.

title: Pebble Dot Friends
lesson: Counting in order from 1 to 10, number names
scene: Ten pale pebbles lie on the sand in a loose shape, and the next one glows yellow. The child taps them in order as the Orbi counts aloud, and a thread of light joins them until a heron appears and flies up.

views.world: The pebble beach in the blue hour after sunset, the sand cool and pale. The river is still and reflects a deep blue sky with the first stars. A white Chord tower glows softly at its crown, and white lattice nests show tiny warm lights in the trees. Peaceful, quiet and a little magical. Top-down camera over the sand.
views.details: Dot pebbles are round and pale, each glowing sunshine yellow when it is next. A thread of light, red to blue like a Link, joins tapped pebbles. Finished shapes become chibi animals: a heron, a turtle, a fish. Verbi, the springy green triangle, hops along the line. A white Orbi floats above, eyes coral red and sky blue.
views.discovery: Pictures start with three dots and grow to ten. Each finished animal comes alive and joins a gentle night parade along the river. Later the child counts back from five to send up a soft burst of tower light, and a free mode lets the child place their own pebbles for Verbi to join.

story: One evening, ten pebbles began to glow on the beach. "Let's join them!" said Verbi. "One!" He hopped to the first. "Two! Three!" Each pebble lit a thread of light to the next. "Four, five, six!" The line bent and curled. "Seven, eight, nine, ten!" The last pebble shone, and the line became a heron. It shook its wings and flew over the river. Verbi waved. "Counting in order made a friend," he said, and the ten pebbles dimmed, ready for tomorrow.
wisdom: One step at a time, and the picture appears.

title: Mixing Puddles
lesson: Primary and mixed colors, cause and effect
scene: Two rain puddles on flat stones shine yellow and blue. The child taps the Orbi, it carries one drop from each into an empty middle puddle, and the water swirls into bright leaf green.

views.world: The pebble beach just after a warm summer rain, every stone wet and shining. Rain puddles sit in hollows of flat white rocks. A rainbow arcs over the river, and a white Chord tower stands beneath it, glistening. The trees drip, and white lattice nests sparkle with drops. The air looks fresh and clean.
views.details: Puddles are round and clear, tinted by the Orbi with a harmless glow color that fades away by evening: coral red, sunshine yellow and sky blue. The white Orbi carries drops with a gentle shimmer. Soru and Tari stand at the edge with little buckets. Mixed colors swirl like marbled paint. Bold gray outlines, big simple shapes.
views.discovery: First two colors make one new color: red and yellow make orange, blue and yellow make green. Later a friend shows a wish, like a green frog who wants a green pond, and the child mixes it. A free mode lets the child splash new colors over a whole beach picture, then watch them fade at sunset.

story: After the rain, Soru found a yellow puddle and Tari found a blue one. "Mine is the best color!" said Soru. "No, mine is!" said Tari. The Orbi carried one drop of yellow and one drop of blue into a puddle between them. The water swirled and turned green, like new leaves. The twins stared. "That is not my color," said Soru, "and not yours." "It is ours," said Tari. They mixed and mixed until the beach was full of colors that no one could make alone.
wisdom: Together we make colors no one makes alone.

title: Mirror Pond Feelings
lesson: Naming feelings, empathy, choosing a kind action
scene: Oopsy looks into a still pond, and his reflection shows a sad face. Three big face pebbles wait below: happy, sad and surprised. The child taps sad, then chooses a hug, and Itsy hugs him.

views.world: A small, round pond beside the river, so still it is a mirror. Ferns and soft moss circle its edge. A blue-green tree leans overhead with a white lattice nest. A white Chord tower is reflected upside down in the water. Soft, late afternoon light with warm golden tones. Close, eye-level camera at the water's edge.
views.details: Oopsy is a small, clumsy chibi robot with a band-aid and a big face. Itsy is an infinity loop that hugs itself, with blushing cheeks. Feeling pebbles show four clear faces: happy, sad, angry and scared, in soft colors. A white Orbi floats near the pond, eyes coral red and sky blue. Moss green, water silver, warm gold.
views.discovery: Feelings grow from happy and sad to angry, scared, surprised and proud. After naming a feeling, the child picks a kind action: a hug, sharing, a quiet rest or a song. Later little scenes show two friends feeling different things at once, and the child helps each one in their own way.

story: Oopsy dropped his favorite pebble into the pond. His face crumpled. He looked into the water and saw his own face, wet and sad. Itsy floated over. "What do you feel?" she asked. "Sad," said Oopsy, very quietly. "That is okay," said Itsy. "Feelings are like weather. They come, and they go." She gave him a hug. Then the Orbi lifted the pebble gently from the water. Oopsy looked into the pond again. Now his face was smiling. "The pond changed," he said. "No," said Itsy, "you did."
wisdom: Name a feeling, and it gets lighter.

title: Story Stones
lesson: Before and after, daily routines, retelling a story
scene: Four flat story stones lie on the beach showing a seed, a sprout, a flower and a bee. The child drags them into a row of hollows, and when the order is right, the story plays as a short voiced cartoon.

views.world: A gentle curve of the pebble beach where a long flat rock holds a row of shallow hollows, like seats for stones. Behind it the river flows, and the trees hold white lattice nests. A white Chord tower stands against a clear sky. Warm morning light and a calm, storybook mood. Front view, low and close.
views.details: Story stones are flat, smooth and oval, each painted with one large, clear picture in soft colors. Choo-Choo Seq, a little caterpillar train whose cars are pairs of friends, curls beside the row. A white Orbi lifts stones with a shimmer, eyes coral red and sky blue. Simple shapes, gray outlines, warm sand and stone tones.
views.discovery: The first stories are a day in a nest: wake up, wash, eat, play and sleep. Then come little nature tales: an egg hatches, a seed grows, rain falls and a puddle dries. Later the child sets four stones in any order, and the Orbi tells a silly new story that matches the child's choice.

story: Choo-Choo Seq found four stones on the beach. One showed a chick waking up. One showed the chick eating. One showed the chick playing. One showed a moon. "Which comes first?" asked Seq. The child set them in a row: wake up, eat, play, and sleep under the moon. Seq rolled along the row, and the stones told the story of a whole day. "Every story has a beginning, a middle and an end," said Seq, "like cars on a train." Then he curled up by the moon stone and fell asleep.
wisdom: Every story has a beginning, middle and end.

title: Pebble Beach Picnic
lesson: Sharing food, one for each friend, plant foods
scene: A white picnic cloth lies on the pebbles with three hungry friends around it. The child drags a copied apple, a berry bowl and a leaf cup to each friend, who munches happily and hums a thank you.

views.world: A wide, sunny pebble beach with a soft white picnic cloth spread near the water. The river sparkles, and an old apple tree on the bank keeps its fruit for the birds. White lattice nests hang in nearby trees, and a white Chord tower rises in the distance. Bright midday light, cheerful and relaxed.
views.details: Linky, Soru, Tari and Verbi sit around the cloth. A garden basket holds copied fruit: apples, berries, pears and flatbread, made overnight by the garden assembler and never picked. A white Orbi floats over the basket, eyes coral red and sky blue. Leaf cups and wooden plates are big and round. Sunny yellow, apple red, leaf green and white.
views.discovery: The first picnic has three friends and simple food. Later more friends arrive, up to ten, and the child sets one plate for each. New picnic spots appear: under a tower, on a sandbar, in a tree nest. A little cooking corner lets the child stir a fruit salad and pour juice, all pretend and all shared.

story: Linky wanted a picnic. He looked at the old apple tree. "May I take one?" he asked. "Copy, don't take," hummed his Orbi. The Orbi scanned an apple and left it on its branch for the birds. In the morning, a basket of copied apples was waiting. Linky spread a white cloth on the pebbles and called his friends. One apple for Soru, one for Tari, one for Verbi, and one for Linky. Everyone munched. A bird pecked the real apple on the tree. "Everybody gets a picnic," said Linky.
wisdom: Copy, don't take, and everyone gets a share.

title: Plush Patch Clinic
lesson: Caring for others, body parts, feeling brave
scene: A plush grazer fawn with a torn ear lies on a soft cushion in a nest clinic. The Orbi scans it with a gentle blue glow, and the child drags a soft patch onto the ear to mend it.

views.world: A cozy white lattice nest high in a riverside tree, set up as a little toy clinic. Round windows show the pebble beach, the river below and a white Chord tower in the distance. Soft afternoon light falls on shelves of cushions, blankets and toys. Warm, calm and caring. Eye-level camera inside the nest.
views.details: Plush patients are soft felt toys: a fawn, a heron, a turtle and a round grazer, with button eyes and stitched seams. Tools are big and friendly: the Orbi's scanning glow, soft patches, a warm blanket, a cup of herb tea. Itsy gives hugs. The white Orbi's coral-red and sky-blue eyes shine kindly. Cream, soft pink and leaf green.
views.discovery: Each plush has one problem at first: a torn seam, a sniffly cold, a lost button. Later plushes have two problems, and the child chooses what to do first. A waiting cushion shows who is next, and mended toys ride home to their nests. A free mode lets the child invent a new plush and its little owie.

story: Little Turtle the plush had a hole in his shell. His stuffing peeked out. "Will it hurt?" he whispered. The Orbi floated close. "First I will only look. May I?" Little Turtle nodded, and the Orbi scanned him with a soft blue glow. "Just a small tear." Itsy held his flipper. The Orbi held the edges together, and a soft patch went on. "All done," said the Orbi. Little Turtle looked at his shell. "I was scared, but you asked me first and told me what you would do."
wisdom: Ask first, and fear gets smaller.

title: Sharing Circle
lesson: Sharing, swapping, taking turns, saying thank you
scene: Friends sit on round blankets in a circle on the beach, each with a few things to share. Verbi shows a thought bubble of a kite. The child drags a spare kite to him, and he gives back a wooden whistle.

views.world: A wide pebble beach where friends lay round woven blankets in a big circle near the water. Baskets and toys rest on the blankets. A white Chord tower stands nearby, and the trees hold white lattice nests with soft ribbons. Warm late afternoon sun and a gentle breeze. A friendly sharing day under an open sky. High, wide camera.
views.details: Linky, Soru, Tari, Verbi and Anya, the shape-shifting star, sit on blankets with toys, copied fruit, seeds and drawings to share. Big thought bubbles show what each friend would like. A white Orbi floats in the middle, eyes coral red and sky blue. There are no coins, prices or counters, only open hands and baskets.
views.discovery: At first each friend wants one thing and gives one thing back. Later friends borrow and return, take turns with one toy, or split one thing between two. Some rounds the child simply gives and receives a thank-you song. A copy corner lets the Orbi make a second toy overnight, so two friends can both play.

story: It was sharing day on the beach. Anya the star had a basket of seeds but wished for a kite. Verbi had two kites but wished for seeds for his garden. "Would you like to swap?" asked Anya. "Yes!" said Verbi, and gave her a kite. She gave him a handful of seeds. Then Linky came with empty hands. "I have nothing to share," he said sadly. "You can share a song," said Anya. Linky sang, and everyone clapped. On Raya nothing is bought. Everyone has something to give.
wisdom: Everyone has something to share.

title: Arrow Stones for Orbi
lesson: Steps in order, directions, early coding
scene: An Orbi waits at one corner of a small grid of sand squares, and Linky waits at the other. The child drags three big arrow stones into a row, taps go, and the Orbi rolls step by step to Linky.

views.world: A smooth patch of beach where round pebbles mark a grid of sand squares, three by three, near the river. Reeds and a few wildflowers grow at its edges. White lattice nests watch from the trees, and a white Chord tower stands tall in the distance. Clear morning light, a playful puzzle mood. Top-down camera over the grid.
views.details: Arrow stones are big flat pebbles with a bold carved arrow shape, colored leaf green for actions. A white Orbi rolls across the grid, its glowing equator pulsing, coral-red and sky-blue eyes bright. Go, Stop and Hop, the traffic-light siblings, cheer from the side. Linky waits at the goal with open red and blue hands.
views.discovery: Grids grow from two squares to four by four, with puddles and sleeping turtles to go around. If a path goes wrong, the Orbi stops, giggles and points back, and the child changes one stone. Later a loop stone repeats a step, and friends wait in different squares to be visited one after another.

story: The Orbi wanted to visit Linky, but it would only roll where the arrows told it. "Forward, forward, turn," said the child, putting down arrow stones. The Orbi rolled forward, forward, and turned, right into a puddle. It giggled. "Splash!" Oopsy waved from the side. "That is how we learn!" The child changed one stone. Forward, turn, forward. The Orbi rolled, turned and rolled again, and stopped right beside Linky. "You showed me the way, step by step," said the Orbi. "Let's link!" said Linky.
wisdom: Big trips are made of little steps.

title: Shape Spotting Walk
lesson: Circles, squares, triangles and rectangles in the world
scene: A wide beach scene shows round pebbles, a pointed fir, a square nest window and two round moons. The Orbi asks for circles, and the child taps a round pebble, which glows coral red and chimes.

views.world: A long panorama of the river beach at golden hour: round pebbles, triangle-shaped fir trees, a square window in a lattice nest, a long rectangle of driftwood and the two round moons, Pim and Pom, in the sky. A white Chord tower points up like a slim triangle. Warm light, long shadows, an inviting walk.
views.details: Soru, the round coral-red blob, leads circle walks, and Tari, the square sky-blue blob, leads square walks. Verbi, the green triangle, helps with triangles. Found shapes glow with a bright outline in their color. A white Orbi floats beside them, eyes coral red and sky blue. Big clear shapes, soft gray outlines.
views.discovery: The first walk finds circles only. Then squares, triangles, rectangles and stars. Later the scenes change: inside a nest, a forest path, a festival night by the tower. A collecting mode lets the child build a picture of a friend from the shapes they found, and the shape names are sung back.

story: Soru, Tari and Verbi went for a walk on the beach. "Let's find shapes like us," said Soru. She found round pebbles and a round moon. Tari found a square window in a nest and a square flat stone. Verbi found a pointy fir tree and the tip of a tower, both triangles. "Shapes are everywhere," said Tari. "The world is full of friends like us," said Verbi. They walked home, and even their nest looked like a happy shape.
wisdom: Look around, shapes are everywhere.

title: Long Stick, Heavy Stone
lesson: Longer and shorter, heavier and lighter, first measuring
scene: Two driftwood sticks lie side by side on the sand, ends lined up. The child taps the longer one. Then a wide leaf balance held by the Orbi tips down under a big pebble, showing it is heavier.

views.world: A breezy part of the pebble beach where driftwood lies bleached and smooth, and stones of every size rest on the sand. The river flows gently, and a white Chord tower rises behind trees with white lattice nests. Bright, clear daylight, a fresh wind and a curious, hands-on mood. Low, close camera.
views.details: Driftwood sticks are pale gray and smooth; pebbles range from tiny to big, in gray, blue and sand colors. The balance is a wide green leaf held in the air by the Orbi's shimmer. Akoren, the tiny glowing acorn, sits on one side to be weighed. The white Orbi floats in the middle, eyes coral red and sky blue.
views.discovery: Comparisons start with two very different things, then closer ones, then three to put in order from short to long. Later the child measures with pebbles laid in a row, counting how many pebbles long a stick is. A tall and short round compares friends, and a full and empty round uses rain cups.

story: Akoren and a little heron argued. "My stick is longer!" said the heron. "My stone is heavier!" said Akoren. The Orbi laughed softly. "Let us check." It laid the sticks side by side, with the ends together. The heron's stick was longer. Then it held a wide leaf like a balance, with Akoren's stone on one side and the heron's feather on the other. The stone went down. "You were both right," said the Orbi. "Long is one way to measure. Heavy is another."
wisdom: Put things side by side to know.

title: One Tree, Four Seasons
lesson: The four seasons, weather, and what nature does in each
scene: A big tree on the riverbank changes with each season. The Orbi shows autumn, and the child drags the matching things into the picture: orange leaves, wind, and geese flying south over the river.

views.world: A single wide tree on a gentle riverbank above the pebble beach, shown four ways: pink spring blossom in soft rain, deep green summer under bright sun, orange autumn with wind and falling leaves, and quiet white winter snow. A white Chord tower stands behind it in every season. Wide, calm and beautiful.
views.details: The tree has a round crown and a small white lattice nest. Season items are big friendly stickers: rain clouds, sun, falling leaves, snowflakes, blossoms, migrating geese, a sleepy fawn. Linky and the white Orbi visit in every season, the Orbi glowing coral red and sky blue. Colors shift from pink to green to orange to white.
views.discovery: First the child matches one season at a time. Then today's weather appears, rainy, windy, sunny or snowy, and the child chooses what Linky needs, like a scarf or a leaf umbrella. Later the seasons turn in order on a big wheel, and animals arrive and leave: birds fly away, fawns are born, frogs sleep.

story: Linky loved his tree by the river. In spring it wore pink flowers, and the rain made puddles. In summer it was green and gave cool shade. In autumn its leaves turned orange and danced away in the wind. "Oh no, my tree is leaving!" said Linky. The Orbi floated close. "It is only resting. Watch." Winter came, and snow covered the branches. Linky waited and waited. Then one morning, a tiny green bud appeared. "Everything comes back in its time," said the Orbi.
wisdom: Everything comes back in its time.
